hints: Read test_kata.py. Each test names one rule: the event name, the joined data, the comments, the end of the text.
Split the text on newlines. Keep the current event name and the data lines until a blank line.

Nearly the code: for a line that is not blank and not a comment, use line.partition(':'). Set event for the field event, append the value for the field data, and drop one leading space from the value.
solution:
def parse_events(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Parse a server-sent events stream (the rules the kata tests) into events."""
    events: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    event = "message"
    data: list[str] = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line == "":  # a blank line ends an event
            if data:
                events.append({"event": event, "data": "\n".join(data)})
            event = "message"
            data = []
            continue
        if line.startswith(":"):  # a comment, such as a keep-alive
            continue
        field, _, value = line.partition(":")
        if value.startswith(" "):  # one space after the colon is not part of the value
            value = value[1:]
        if field == "event":
            event = value
        elif field == "data":
            data.append(value)
    return events

def parse_events(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Parse a server-sent events stream into events, each {"event": ..., "data": ...}.

    Rules: a line "field: value" sets a field; drop one space after the colon.
    "event" names the event (default "message"); each "data" line adds one line
    to the data. Lines starting with ":" are comments and are skipped. A blank
    line ends an event, and only an event with data is returned. An event
    that has no blank line after it at the end of the text is not returned.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("split the text into lines, and collect the fields until a blank line")
